text:
frank: Quick kickoff  I want a compact roadmap canvas for long-term routing (multi-region + tenant isolation). Sales wants a one-pager they can hand prospects; infra needs concrete gates. Can we agree a naming convention for phases and crisp launch criteria?

emily: Love the idea. Propose three customer-visible phases with distinct guarantees: Prism (proof), Rampart (operational), Fortress (commercial-grade). Keep language non-legal until Legal blesses it.

sana: Drafted an outline in-thread to iterate:
- Prism (0-45d): policy knobs (latency/cost/geo), tenant hints, minimal affinity. No SLA.
- Rampart (45-180d): tenant lanes, reserved pools, 7d live canary, runbook + automated fallback. Eligible for SLOs after gating.
- Fortress (180d+): full policy DSL, multi-region active-active, hardened eviction semantics, fine-grained residency controls. Commercial SLA available.

keiko: Ops gating checklist (short bullets): emitted telemetry schema, runbook drill executed, compatibility matrix published, canary pass (>=7d), and rollback automation. Also add a hysteresis rule for auto-fallback to avoid noisy flips.

tom: Sales asks mapped to phases: Prism = demoable behavior (policy examples), Rampart = "eligible for SLA" & reserved-pool offer with commit, Fortress = contractual SLA + jurisdictional attestation. Need exact gating language for contracts.

legal-bot: Note: legal review required for any wording that implies guaranteed uptime. Use "eligible for SLA" not "SLA provided" until contracts signed.

sana: Canary proposal: two-region pairs, 7 days live at 5% traffic, synthetic load before live ramp, failure criteria: p95/p99 degradation > 15% OR error-rate delta > 1% sustained for 10m. Canary must include KV parity tests with reconciliation window <= 1h.

frank: Good. Ops: what's the minimal telemetry contract we need? Keep it tiny so infra can emit fast.

keiko: Minimal events: routing.event.policy_decide (tenant,policy_id,reason), routing.event.route_pick (tenant,region,latency_ms), routing.event.fallback (tenant,reason), routing.event.kv_reconcile (tenant,status). Each must include tenant_id & policy_id. Emit at INFO tier for canary.

infra-bot: Perf-harness note: we can run the canary against eu-us and apac-us pairs. It needs a compatibility matrix to select model families that are runnable in lanes.

sana: Compatibility spike scope (owner: infra): produce a 2-week matrix for top 6 model families across quant formats and accelerated kernels with p50/p95/p99 delta and cost uplift. This is gating for Rampart pricing.

frank: Pricing: finance will need uplift bands tied to compatibility scores. For product collateral let's show example bands (illustrative): score 2 = +15-25%, score 3 = +30-50%. Finance to confirm.

tom: Operational safety: define eviction flow in the canvas. Example order: 1) reduce batch size & aspiration, 2) degrade to fallback model family, 3) drain to global pool with controlled spill fraction. Provide policy fields for soft/hard thresholds.

sana: Example policy snippet for customer docs (display-only):
```
{
  "policy_id": "pref_region_v1",
  "priorities": ["jurisdiction","latency"],
  "regions": ["eu-west1","us-west1"],
  "fallback": {"type":"global_pool","max_spill":0.05},
  "eviction": {"soft_fraction":0.75,"hard_fraction":0.95}
}
```
Use this in the one-pager to show semantics.

keiko: Add SLI for auto-fallback hysteresis: require 2 consecutive evaluation ticks (5m each) plus a 10m sustained window before auto-fallback triggers. Also add an operator confirmation step for high-impact tenants when not in canary.

legal-bot: Also include a non-binding note: "Actual SLA availability contingent on customer commitments (capacity, tenancy restrictions) and final contract terms."

frank: Good flag. Let's also capture customer stories that unlock revenue so PM can prioritize. Emily, can you list top 3?

emily: Top asks from field: 1) per-region data residency (legal/regulatory), 2) dedicated capacity for predictable throughput (enterprise), 3) deterministic p99 tail latency for latency-sensitive features. All feed Rampart/Fortress.

sana: Action items:
- infra: compatibility spike (2 weeks) -> deliver matrix and cost uplifts (owner: infra)
- sana: one-pager canvas with Prism/Rampart/Fortress, canary plan, telemetry list, sample policy, and gating bullets (3 business days)
- keiko: runbook drill template + auto-fallback SLI text (5 business days)
- tom: coordinate with finance to draft illustrative uplift bands (5 business days)

infra-bot: Canary scheduler: perf-run queued for eu-us pair tomorrow 08:00 UTC. Owner: infra.

keiko: Ops note  ensure "policy_decide" events include a routing_decision_id so we can trace from decision -> chosen host -> logs. This helps debugging during canary.

frank: When the one-pager is ready, we'll do a 30m review with sales and legal present. Key metric: can we get two enterprise prospects to sign within 60d of Rampart availability? If yes, prioritize.

emily: One more collateral idea: include a short FAQ on "what we do when a lane overloads" and "how pricing is calculated". Keep it 3 bullets each. Sales likes simple answers.

sana: I'll post the draft canvas in #product and tag legal + sales once ready. Any final asks?

tom: Please avoid promising exact RTOs in marketing language until legal signs off. Stick to "eligible for SLA" phrasing.

frank: Thanks all. Let's keep the canvas lean and actionable. Sana will post by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
